title: Lead Anyway: 10 Rules for Leading When You Break the Mold
description: In a corporate world still shaped by outdated ideals of charisma and conformity, Lead Anyway offers a new model for leadership from the margins. Drawing on her experience as a senior executive, neurodivergent professional, and global keynote speaker, Laurence Paquette delivers ten clear rules for leading without pretending to be someone you’re not. Combining personal narrative, leadership research, and practical tools, the book challenges performative leadership and replaces it with a more honest, sustainable approach to influence. title: Lead Anyway: The Human Side of School Leadership
description: Leadership is heavier than anyone prepares you for. This book is for the leaders who stay anyway. Lead Anyway: The Human Side of School Leadership is not a how-to manual or a collection of leadership hacks. It is an honest, grounded exploration of what leadership actually asks of you when the building is tired, trust is thin, and the weight of responsibility does not clock out at the end of the day. Drawing from lived experience as an award-winning school leader, Dr. Edwin Garcia, Jr. names the invisible work leaders carry every day. The emotional labor. The quiet decisions. The moments between meetings that shape culture more than any plan ever could. This book speaks directly to principals, assistant principals, instructional leaders, and aspiring school administrators who know leadership is not just technical, but deeply human. Inside, you will explore: Why leadership feels heavier than expected and why that weight matters How belief, self-trust, and presence anchor leaders through uncertainty What it means to lead adults first so students can succeed How trust is built quietly through consistency, listening, and integrity Leading without ego, urgency, or performance-driven authority Staying human in a role that often hardens people Protecting what works during change, fatigue, and transition Each chapter blends reflection, real leadership moments, and grounded insight without pretending leadership is clean or predictable. This is not a book about perfection. It is a book about presence. Lead Anyway is for leaders who: Care deeply but feel tired Question themselves but keep showing up Want language for what they already feel Believe leadership is about people, not just systems If you are looking for step-by-step formulas, this book may frustrate you. title: Lead Anyway: How to Build the Career You Want When the Rules Weren’t Written for You
description: In Lead Anyway , Jen Spencer draws from over twenty years of unconventional career pivots, real-world executive leadership, and lived experience across education, nonprofit theatre, SaaS, and the C-suite to deliver a refreshingly honest roadmap for modern leaders. This book isn’t another corporate playbook; it’s a masterclass in leading with authenticity, empathy, and the kind of hard-won clarity that only comes from stepping off the traditional path. Through raw stories, practical insights, and deeply relatable moments from building programs that were taken away without warning, to navigating acquisitions, to finding her voice in rooms where she was the only woman, Jen reveals what leadership really looks like when the script runs out. Blending lived lessons with actionable tools, Lead Anyway helps leaders at every stage build confidence, trust themselves, speak up, and lead from who they are, not who they were told to be. Whether you're an emerging leader or an executive shaping company-wide impact, this book gives you the clarity and courage to stop waiting for permission and start leading on your own terms. Lead Anyway will help you: • Embrace nonlinear growth and turn pivots, pauses, and reinvention into your leadership advantage. • Translate every skill you already have from teaching to tech, from creativity to strategy into powerful leadership currency. • Build the confidence to speak up, even in rooms where louder voices dominate. • Understand the truth about impostor syndrome and learn to turn doubt into data, direction, and self-trust. • Cultivate emotional intelligence, empathy, and presence so you can lead people—not just manage outcomes. • Start before you feel “ready,” make brave decisions, and navigate uncertainty without losing yourself. title: Lead Anyway: The Glow-Up Guide to Leadership That’s Real, Not Perfect
description: THIS ISN’T A “HOW TO LEAD LIKE A CEO” BOOK. It’s a “how to lead when your kid’s lunch isn’t made and you’re still wearing yesterday’s mascara” book. Lead Anyway: The Glow-Up Guide to Leadership That’s Real, Not Perfect is for every woman who has ever doubted she was a leader and still showed up. It’s a mix of real stories, hard truths, and the kind of pep talks you’d get from your smartest, funniest friend who says the things we are all thinking. Dr. Lauren Young pulls back the curtain on what leadership actually looks like: messy, brave, and exhausting, but those who are committed to it keep showing up. Because you don’t need another guru or serum. You need a reminder that you can glow up and screw up—and still be a darn good leader. You don’t have to be perfect. Blending personal anecdotes, hard-earned wisdom, and insightful reflections, the book takes readers behind the scenes of the school system-from the classroom to the boardroom. title: She Leads Anyway: A Guide for Women and Youth Who Dare to Lead
description: Leadership does not begin with a title, position, or permission. It begins with the courage to believe in yourself and take the first step. She Leads Anyway is an empowering guide for women and young people who are ready to discover their potential, overcome self-doubt, and make a meaningful difference. Through personal experiences and practical wisdom, Dr. Sylvia Litana Ezozo encourages readers to embrace their voices, recognize their strengths, and lead with purpose. Drawing from her remarkable journey from Ndola, Zambia, to international leadership and community development, Dr. Ezozo shares powerful lessons about resilience, identity, courage, and personal growth. She explores the challenges of leadership, including rejection, criticism, gender barriers, cultural expectations, and the fear of being seen. Through stories of mentorship, entrepreneurship, diaspora engagement, and women's empowerment, she demonstrates how leadership can create opportunities, strengthen communities, and inspire future generations. Whether you are an aspiring leader, a young professional, an entrepreneur, or a woman seeking the confidence to step into your purpose, this book offers encouragement and practical insights for your journey. Learn to use your voice, build meaningful relationships, develop your leadership abilities, and create opportunities for others. You do not need perfect circumstances to begin, and you do not need everyone's approval to make an impact. Your journey matters, your voice matters, and your leadership matters. You can lead anyway! Discover Your Leadership Potential: Build confidence, self-awareness, and the courage to step forward. Overcome Barriers: Navigate criticism, rejection, stereotypes, and self-doubt with resilience. title: Lead Anyway: The Truth About Grit, Growth, and Getting It Wrong First
description: The Truth About Grit, Growth, and Getting It Wrong First Leadership isn’t clean. It isn’t comfortable. And it rarely comes with certainty. Lead Anyway is a raw, unfiltered memoir of leadership forged through failure, service, sacrifice, and relentless perseverance. Drawing from a life shaped by combat deployments, law enforcement, fatherhood, and personal collapse, William Long Jr. challenges the polished myths of leadership and replaces them with something far more honest: presence, accountability, and the courage to keep going when everything falls apart. This is not a motivational handbook filled with clichés. It’s a field manual for the tired, the burned out, and the ones carrying weight no one sees . From growing up with quiet hardship, to serving in Afghanistan after 9/11, to rebuilding life as a single father while wearing the uniform, this book tells the truth most leadership books avoid— that the best leaders are often the ones who felt least prepared . Through powerful real-life stories and reflective “Leadership Debriefs,” Lead Anyway explores: Leading through failure, doubt, and fear Carrying responsibility without recognition Choosing integrity when it costs comfort Balancing duty, family, and personal survival Showing up when quitting would be easier This book is for: Veterans, Soldiers, and first responders Leaders without titles Parents carrying silent burdens Professionals burned out by expectations Anyone rebuilding after life went off-script If you’ve ever questioned your worth, doubted your ability, or felt like leadership came to you before you were ready—this book is your reminder: You don’t lead because you’re perfect. title: Lead Anyway: Teaching Through the Fog When the System Stops Seeing You
description: You didn't leave. That already says something about who you are. You entered education to make a difference — and you still believe that. Even now, when the emotional weight has become something no job description prepared you for. When resources shrank and expectations expanded. When the recognition faded but the responsibility didn't. When you started wondering if the system even sees you anymore. You still show up. You still care. You are still leading — even if no one has called it that. Lead Anyway was written for that educator. Award-winning author Dr. Karissa Thomas draws from years of research and practice inside educational systems to offer teachers, instructional coaches, school leaders, department chairs, and higher education faculty a framework for leading with clarity, composure, and steady influence — even when the institution feels unclear, unsupported, or unjust. This is not a book about surviving the system. It is a book about leading within it — with presence, purpose, and the kind of quiet authority that shapes school culture long before any title is ever assigned. title: Lead Anyway: Lessons From The Second Man
description: You won’t always get a second swing. But you can lead like you’ve already learned the lesson. Lead Anyway introduces the Second Man Theory - a practical mindset that helps leaders reflect faster, act bolder, and show up with clarity the first time, not just the second. Drawing on over 30 years of real-world leadership - including military service in both the U.S. Marine Corps and Navy -Tracy Askew offers a leadership framework built on experience, resilience, and reflection. This isn’t theory from the sidelines. It’s honest, no-fluff guidance from someone who’s led under pressure, made the mistakes, and found the insight on the other side. Inside you’ll learn how to: Lead through chaos with calm and direction Build trust without waiting to feel “ready” Give feedback that strengthens rather than shatters Clarify vision early, not after the fact Prepare others to carry the mission forward Each chapter includes Second Man Reflections - real-time prompts that help you course-correct and lead with more wisdom and conviction, right now. Whether you're new to leadership or carrying the weight of a team, Lead Anyway is both a mirror and a toolbox.
